The *Nāgasamālattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 73) is a canonical verse text preserved in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like other poems in this collection, it presents the biographical verses associated with the elder (thera) Nāgasamāla. Five translations in five languages are documented in modern collections [SuttaCentral].

Neither SuttaCentral nor the automated DharmaNexus database records external cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan traditions [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon and its commentarial literature, however, DharmaNexus identifies widespread formulaic reuse, detecting 66 matching passages across 28 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Significant portions of its verses are shared with other poems of the Therāpadāna, including the *Tamālapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 193, sharing §1.3–5.1), the *Udakāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 233), and the *Bhojanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 314) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, segments of the poem (§4.1–5.1) correspond directly to passages quoted in the commentary on the Theragāthā (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus].
